extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys and agents), respondents in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order setting out the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct violations, mitigating/aggravating factors, required sanctions, and post‑sanction duties for a registered patent practitioner. It specifies what conduct violated the rules and the remedial, reporting, education, and reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — Competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to provide competent representation to a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of competence failures listed: failing to notify the client of the Notice to File Corrected Application Papers, notice of insufficient funds, Notice of Incomplete Reply, and Notice of Abandonment; failing to properly respond to the Notice to File Corrected Application Papers; failing to respond to the notice of insufficient funds and Notice of Incomplete Reply; allowing the application to become abandoned without the client's consent; failing to take steps to revive the abandoned application; failing to explain to the client the significance of the abandoned application, the standard for filing a petition for revival, the significance of patent term adjustment, and how the practitioner's actions and delay may affect the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to notify the client of important USPTO notices for extended periods (e.g., ~18 months for the Notice to File Corrected Application Papers, ~11 months for notices of insufficient funds, Incomplete Reply, and Abandonment); failing to properly respond to Office communications; failing to take steps to revive the abandoned application for approximately 11 months after abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104 — Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the client's matter (37 C.F.R. § 11.104).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific failures noted: not informing the client about Office notices for extended periods (18 months or ~11 months), failing to inform the client what actions had occurred in the application, and allowing the client to believe everything was okay when it was not. The Order treats timely, accurate communication about Office actions and application status as a required duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — Dishonesty / Misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order treats as misrepresentation failing to inform the client about Office communications and allowing the client to believe the application was fine; when the respondent did inform the client, he 'merely stated that he had made a mistake' without explaining the exact nature of the events (e.g., that an extension fee payment was returned for insufficient funds and that the application had been abandoned for ~11 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete example: submitting a $750 extension fee payment to the USPTO when the practitioner knew, or should have known, that he did not have sufficient funds in his bank account, resulting in a rejected payment and subsequent abandonment. Financial mismanagement that interferes with Office processes is treated as prejudicial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to advise clients about abandonment, revival, and patent term consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must inform and counsel clients about the significance of an abandoned application, the standard for filing a petition for revival, the significance of patent term adjustment, and how delays/actions may affect the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists failing to explain these matters as part of competence and communication violations. Adequate counsel includes timely explanation of Office actions and consequences and counseling in time to permit client to take appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to ensure timely and honored fee payments / sound financial management
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must ensure payments submitted to the USPTO are honored (sufficient funds) and must take steps to prevent returned payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent had $215.61 when submitting a $750 payment, which was returned for insufficient funds and led to abandonment. The practitioner later 'consulted with his bank ... to prevent future payments being returned' and reconciled accounts. The Order treats submission of payments without sufficient funds as misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation reporting obligations (agreed sanctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: During an 18‑month probation, respondent must submit a written report to the OED Director every 6 months containing specified information about applications affected by insufficient funds payments or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required report items (to be provided at 6, 12, 18 months) include: (1) identity by application number of each U.S. patent application where an Office payment was not honored for insufficient funds or respondent learned a payment was not honored; (2) whether/how/when respondent reported the notice of insufficient funds to the client; (3) documentary evidence corroborating that respondent reported in writing; (4) actions respondent communicated to client and actions taken to rectify the payment; (5) documentary evidence corroborating actions taken; (6) identity by application number of each utility application where a Notice of Abandonment was issued during probation predicated on failure to file timely/complete/proper response; (7) whether/how/when respondent reported the Office communication to the client prior to abandonment; (8) documentary evidence corroborating that report; (9) whether/how/when respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment to the client; (10) whether/how/when respondent counseled the client about the abandonment, including whether counsel occurred in adequate time to avoid abandonment; (11) documentary evidence corroborating reporting and counseling; (12) for each application where respondent did not counsel in adequate time, identify application number, client name/address, and detailed explanation why counseling did not occur in time; (13) if none, a statement that there are no such applications to report in that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific duties and responsibilities a suspended practitioner must perform under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires: (1) provide notice of suspension to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies where admitted; (2) provide notice to all clients with immediate or prospective business before the Office and make appropriate arrangements for legal services; (3) provide notice of suspension to practitioners for opposing parties (or parties if unrepresented) in matters pending before the Office; (4) not hold oneself out as authorized to practice before the Office until reinstated; (5) not render legal advice/services to any person having immediate or prospective business before the Office until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to certain duties during suspension (90‑day reinstatement window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a petition for reinstatement is not granted within 90 days, the suspended practitioner is not required to perform certain duties spelled out in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists duties the respondent does not have to perform unless not reinstated within 90 days: (1) file a notice of withdrawal in each pending application; (2) deliver to all clients documents specified by the regulation; (3) relinquish to client or designated practitioner all funds for practice before the Office, including unearned fees and unexpended advanced costs; (4) remove telephone/legal/directory advertisements stating availability; (5) change any existing advertising regarding availability or ability to perform legal services for persons with business before the Office; (6) change office signs or stationery to delete representations suggesting authorization to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance content (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon compliance with suspension requirements, respondent must provide an affidavit of compliance with specified appended materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must certify compliance and append: (1) a copy of each form of notice, the names/addresses of clients, practitioners, courts, agencies to which notices were sent, and all return receipts or returned mail received up to the date of the affidavit (per § 11.58(b)(2)(i)); (2) a list of all other State, Federal, and administrative jurisdictions to which the practitioner is admitted (per § 11.58(b)(2)(v)). The Order also lists items the affidavit need not append (e.g., schedules of bank accounts, schedules describing disposition of client/fiduciary funds, proof of distribution of funds, or an affidavit describing steps taken to remove certain advertisements) unless requested by OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must enroll, complete and receive CLE credit for at least one course focused on client communication and trust accounts/ethics/bank accounts, and provide proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and proof: (1) within six months from the Final Order date, enroll in and complete CLE under Minnesota State Bar rules for at least one course whose primary subject matters are (i) communication with clients and (ii) trust accounts, managing clients' money, and/or ethics and bank accounts; (2) within seven months provide OED Director corroborating proof of successful completion including documentary evidence of attendance/completion, a description of course content for which credit was received, and a copy of all written materials provided to participants or other corroborating proof acceptable to the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions and procedural requirements to petition for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO after suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall not resume practice until reinstated by OED Director/USPTO Director per § 11.60(a). After suspension and compliance with § 11.58, respondent may file a petition for reinstatement per § 11.60(b), which must be filed with OED Director accompanied by the required fee per § 11.60(c). Any petition must comply with applicable provisions of §§ 11.60(c)(1)-(3) and must attest to compliance with § 11.58, including a sworn declaration that the practitioner has not practiced before the Office during suspension. The OED need not publish notice of the petition per § 11.60(g) as applied here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction enforcement procedure and potential additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure if OED Director believes respondent violated the Agreement, Final Order, or USPTO Rules during probation, including Orders to Show Cause and possible additional suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OED Director believes respondent failed to comply, the Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why USPTO Director should not immediately suspend respondent for up to an additional five months for the violations set forth; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to respondent at last address of record; (C) grant respondent fifteen days to respond. If after the 15‑day period the OED Director continues to believe respondent failed to comply, the OED Director will deliver to the USPTO Director (i) the Order to Show Cause; (ii) respondent's response, if any; and (iii) argument/evidence supporting the OED Director's position, and request that the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending respondent for up to an additional five months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish the Final Order and the Office shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension and Probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order will be electronically published at the OED FOIA Reading Room URL and the OED Director will publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the notice text included in the Final Order, which summarizes findings, the suspension/probation imposed, the Rules violated, factual background (e.g., rejected payment, abandonment, inadequate communication), and mitigation factors considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in mitigation/aggravation for settlement & sanction determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office considered factors in reaching the settlement and determining sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed considerations include: respondent accepted responsibility for his actions; respondent expressed contrition and understands seriousness of actions; respondent had no prior discipline in 16 years of practice; respondent provided full and fair disclosures to OED during the investigation. The Order also notes these findings may be used as aggravating/mitigating factors in future proceedings.
